title: feat: allow account-scoped media upload IDs
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds optional `id` to `POST /upload` for multipart and JSON; omitting it preserves random IDs.
- Scopes custom IDs to the account, uses atomic create-only R2 writes, and returns `409` on duplicates. Gallery entries reserve their IDs until deleted.
- Serves custom-ID files with `no-store`. Adds no endpoints, database tables, or cache-backend changes.
- Clarifies create-only retries, non-deletable unlisted files, read-refreshed expiry, partial-failure conflicts, and public URL discoverability in Scalar/OpenAPI and the media guide.
- Independent adversarial/simplicity reviews completed by Codex and Fable 5.1; no demonstrated blockers after contract clarification. All 39 media tests pass. Biome and Worker bundle check pass; existing catalog/Drizzle typecheck errors remain.

gist.headline: Name your own pixels
gist.blurb: Media uploads can now carry an ID you choose, scoped neatly to your account. The hive will guard that name until its gallery entry is gone.
gist.summary: POST /upload now accepts an optional account-scoped custom id for multipart and JSON uploads, using atomic create-only R2 writes and returning 409 when an existing file or gallery entry already reserves that id.
gist.impact: Developers can create stable, memorable media URLs without coordinating random upload IDs, while duplicate custom IDs are safely rejected and custom-ID responses use no-store caching.
gist.visual_concept: Depict custom media IDs as hand-written labels being attached to glowing pixel image jars in a cozy garden archive. Polli acts as the careful librarian, placing a unique label on one jar while a small retro terminal displays a friendly 409 duplicate sign beside an already-reserved jar; include vines and code-plants to show account-scoped organization.
gist.image_prompt: A cozy pixel-art garden archive where the cute pixel art bee mascot with a yellow body and dark brown horizontal stripes, small black legs, two black antennae, black vertical oval eyes, bright pink rectangular blush marks on cheeks, a small happy smile, and small rounded light blue translucent wings wears tiny librarian glasses and carefully labels glowing media jars with unique account tags; a retro terminal beside one already-labeled jar shows small pixel text “409”. Cozy 8-bit pixel art aesthetic, soft lime green (#ecf874) and pastel gradient background, code-plants and flowers, chunky retro sprites, warm lighting, lo-fi vibes like Stardew Valley or A Short Hike, nostalgic but beautiful.
